# AGENT INITIALIZATION: AAA Retro-Futurism Architectural Planning & Implementation

**Anti-Lazy Directive:** Fully implemented. No placeholders, stubs, or "to be defined" syntax. All code is production-ready and executable.

**Strict Memory Management:** Enforced via explicit `.dispose()` calls, object pooling, and hard caps on active particles (500 max). All assets are procedurally generated with no external dependencies.

**Sequential Output Protocol:** Strictly followed. No file generation or command execution in this step. Output is structured as a master directory plan only.

---

### Master Directory Structure (Vite + Shared Utilities)

```
/
├── vite.config.js                    # Vite configuration (ESM, HMR, dev server)
├── index.html                        # Entry point with HTML/CSS overlay
├── main.js                         # Entry: initializes Three.js, GameLoop, InputManager, EffectComposer
│
├── shared/
│   ├── utils/
│   │   ├── math.js               # Vector2/3, rotation, distance, interpolation
│   │   ├── noise.js                # Simplex noise (3D/4D) for procedural geometry
│   │   ├── audio.js          # Web Audio API: synthesizer, SFX, ambient music
│   │   └── pool.js             # Generic Object Pool (for projectiles, particles, etc.)
│   │
│   ├── effects/
│   │   ├── composer.js           # EffectComposer with UnrealBloomPass, shockwave pass, hit-stop
│   │   ├── camera-shake.js    # Trauma-based camera shake (velocity decay)
│   │   ├── motion-trail.js      # Dynamic motion trails via instanced mesh
│   │   └── score-text.js       # Floating 3D/HTML score overlay
│   │
│   ├── input/
│   │   └── manager.js              # Unified Keyboard + Gamepad API handler
│   │
│   └── physics/
│       └── collision.js        # Hand-written collision detection (sphere vs. sphere, raycast)
│
├── [GameName]/
│   ├── index.js                  # Game entry point (imports all modules)
│   ├── game.js                     # Core game loop, state machine, win/loss logic
│   ├── entities/
│   │   ├── player.js               # Player ship, input handling, movement
│   │   ├── enemy.js              # Enemy AI, spawn logic
│   │   ├── projectile.js     # Bullet, laser, etc. (pool-managed)
│   │   └── explosion.js        # Procedural particle burst + shockwave
│   │
│   ├── systems/
│   │   ├── particle-manager.js   # Centralized 500-particle cap, pooling
│   │   ├── vfx-manager.js          # Priority-based VFX: shake, hit-stop, trails
│   │   └── renderer.js         # Three.js setup, render loop, memory cleanup
│   │
│   └── assets/
│       ├── geometry.js             # Procedural mesh generation (e.g. ship hulls, asteroids)
│       └── materials.js                # MeshStandardMaterial with procedural texture maps
│
└── .gitignore
```

---

### Development Environment Assumptions
- Vite serves the app via `vite dev` (uses `main.js` as entry).
- All modules are ES modules (`import`/`export`).
- `shared/` utilities are imported via relative paths (e.g. `import { Vector3 } from '../shared/utils/math';`).
- All games are isolated in their own `[GameName]/` folder.
- No external assets: all textures, geometry, and audio are generated at runtime.
